prior_importants.description: A refused tell can only come from the operator's `pup conductor tell`. Worker idle notices reach the conductor through Claude Code's peer socket (`notify_when_idle`) and never call `tellConductor`. So the clock still starts at the first `pup status` / `pup ui` look, and an operator who only runs `pup status` sees nothing on the first look after hours of blockage.

process_issues.description: Round 4 limits the roster to importants-only reviewers. The delta 6e5b44e..2177352 changes only prose: ADR 0168 lines 42-45 and one comment at conductor.service.ts:397. No real logic changed, no trust boundary or workflow was touched, no source change could trip a guard, and there is no spec source. So none of correctness, security, guards, workflow-safety or spec met its gate, and no reviewer was spawned. docs, conventions, context, simplicity and maintainability are skipped by the round-4 budget. The orchestrator read the delta itself. HEAD equals the PR's headRefOid (2177352d).

The prior important at conductor.service.ts:394-398 is resolved by narrowing the documentation, not by changing behavior. The comment and ADR 0168 now say that only the operator's `pup conductor tell` starts the clock on a refusal, and that otherwise it starts at the first `pup status` / `pup ui` / `pup dashboard` look that finds the box not empty. That matches the code: conductorBlock is called from dashboard.service.ts:107 and noteConductorBox from tellConductor.
